summary: Two married legislators keep separate homes near each other, and one later retires after redistricting puts them in different districts.
realLife: Two married Minnesota legislators kept separate homes, he in a St. Paul apartment near hers, and one later retired after redistricting put them in different districts. He said that children starting school was a reason to want one home for the family.
gates: {the spouse} holds a seat on a body that sits away from home.
Both partners hold seats, or one is about to give theirs up.
weights: Whether a young child is about to start school.
Whether the districts are redrawn so the two no longer share one.
inGame: Households and partnerships, two seats held by members of one household, a young child at home. needs: redistricting that ends a shared district.

turns.what: The couple keep one family home and one of them commutes to the capital.
turns.pulledBy: A young child at home and the cost of a second home.
turns.writesBack: One household, one seat at a distance.

turns.what: Redistricting puts them in different districts and one retires.
turns.pulledBy: The new map and the household's wishes.
turns.writesBack: A seat given up and the household's job record.
